flags.detail: Pre-merge audit found the House skill audit (a required CI check in all 9 members) failing on the sherlock branches. Five SKILL bodies grew past their limit from the sherlock doctrine edits — sheleg-design 4275→5703 and task-pipeline 4607→5429 are HARD breaches of the 5000 budget; super-ux ux-audit 4304→4882, ux-flows 4229→4809 and agent-sync 4506→4765 are past the 4750 working limit. Four references crossed 100 lines without a '## Contents' list, and evidence-docs/GENERATED.md is unreachable from its SKILL.md. The member gates never caught this: npm test does not run the house auditor. Recorded as HOUSE-01..07, each blocking its repo's merge. __pycache__ BUNDLE_NESTED hits are untracked local artifacts, not a debt.

The House skill audit is a required check in all nine members and it was failing every sherlock branch. Two causes, both real: (1) the sherlock doctrine edits grew five SKILL bodies past their limits — fixed by splitting into bundled references, HOUSE-01..07; (2) the PINNED auditor ran without a tokenizer and issued a token verdict from a chars/3.9 ESTIMATE, gapping seven skills that are all under the limit when actually measured. That is the defect the auditor itself names (FIX-MS-01.01). The pin moved to make-skill@5ca5c36 and every member CI now installs tiktoken, so the budget is MEASURED. Two guards (fix-vd-04.01, sloplint) were changed to read the RESOLVED BUNDLE rather than SKILL.md alone, because reading one file made the house rule's own remedy delete the doctrine those guards protect.

main is branch-protected in the members: a release commit cannot be pushed directly, so each release goes out as its own PR and the ANNOTATED tag (B-93) lands on the merge commit. Also recorded: the version bumper must never rewrite a dated record — docs/evidence/, audits/ and retro.md are excluded, because a ledger section states what was true AT a version and rewriting it is falsifying history. super-ux's ledger guard proved this by refusing the tree.

A version bumper that replaces every occurrence rewrites dated records and historical prose. Caught twice by the repos themselves: super-ux's ledger guard refused a rewritten section heading, and telegram-dev's prose ("both manifests declared X until v0.1.11") would have been falsified. The bumper now skips docs/evidence/, audits/ and retro.md entirely, and within a file replaces only where the version is DECLARED — a JSON version field, a VERSION assignment, or a line that declares nothing else. It also derives the CHANGELOG heading shape from the repo.

task-pipeline: the sherlock retrospective work reworded the cold-retirement trigger from "five run stamps" to "five exposure opportunities", and the guard enforcing that the condition names BOTH units was keyed to the old words. It did not fail — its corpus predicate matched nothing, every surface dropped out, and it passed everything. Found only because a negative self-test refused to plant. Fixed by building both the discovery predicate and the assertion from one _COLD_UNITS pattern, so they cannot disagree about scope; the failure message no longer names a unit, because naming one is what tied it to a wording. Committed as 0207e2a with both polarities verified.

Measured against the MERGED mains, not the branches: 210 audit-regression suites across the nine members, 0 red. The umbrella gate on main: 84 suites, 970 fixtures, 9 pinned members, EXIT=0. Open issues across the whole family: ZERO. Open PRs: sshlg-skills#123 (this ledger branch, now merged up to main and green) and task-pipeline#87 with its superseded #85.

A tag is not a release and a release is not a publish, so all three were checked separately for the eight members released today. GitHub releases: all 8 exist and their release.yml runs concluded SUCCESS. npm: all 8 serve the released version — super-ux 0.56.0, seo-aeo-audit 0.26.0, telegram-dev 0.2.0, agent-stack 0.24.0, sheleg-dev 0.12.0, agent-sync 1.20.0, make-skill 0.28.0, sheleg-design-skill 1.60.0. Note for the next reader: super-ux and sheleg-design-skill publish UNSCOPED, so `npm view @ssheleg/super-ux` returns nothing and reads as a failed publish — it is not.

task-pipeline requires the CHANGELOG to state `Guards: N → M`, and refuses a number that disagrees with the workflow. My grep said 432, the validator said 429 — its regex anchors on `^\s*- name:` and mine matched three mentions inside quoted text. The validator was right. The real answer is 429 → 429: no guard was added, three plants were REPOINTED to follow their subjects to the wording those subjects had moved to.

Moving the eight pins in a throwaway branch BEFORE the real pin commit surfaced two things the umbrella would have failed on. (1) The README table is the third place the pin lives and the validator refuses it when skills.json and the table disagree — the pin script now moves all three. (2) Two members shipped a release whose evidence ledger still described the previous version (agent-stack, sheleg-design), against an umbrella ratchet of 1. The ratchet is lowered when a member catches up and NEVER raised to match a regression, and it says why it does not simply fail: only that member's own release can move its ledger. Both caught up in patch releases — agent-stack#29 v0.24.1, sheleg-design#32 v1.60.1. Also confirmed working: my own CTX-04.06 acceptance receipt refused the tree with "receipt disagrees with a fresh staging run (pins moved under it)", which is exactly what it was written to do.

The two ledger-catch-up patches (agent-stack v0.24.1, sheleg-design v1.60.1) SHIPPED STILL LAGGING: the release script wrote the ledger section and then bumped the version, so the section named the version being replaced and the lag it existed to close survived its own fix. Caught by re-running the pin dry-run, which still listed both members. Fixed properly in v0.24.2 / v1.60.2 — bump FIRST, then write the section against what is now declared — and the ordering rule is now a comment at the top of the release script rather than something to remember. Separately, the README step of the pin script had been lost to nested heredocs and is now its own file.

The final sweep caught task-pipeline red on main: v1.86.0 was TAGGED and its release.yml FAILED, so the tag exists, the GitHub release does not, and npm never served it. Cause: the run-stamp gate reads the tag OWN tree and a branch push cannot see a tag that does not exist yet — the seventh instance of a mechanism that repo's retro.md names six times, and its R-010 already held the rule ("run the suite the RELEASE runs, against the tree you are about to tag"). The lesson was written and read past. Fixing it in v1.86.1 surfaced two more: the ledger header must bump in the same change as the version, and moving the conditionals check to a one-line `run:` made the step INVISIBLE to negatives.py (which parses `run: |`), silently emptying the property-check category from 15 to 14 — its own floor caught it. Also learned: GitHub's 512,000 limit is BYTES, and em dashes in a comment cost more than the characters suggest (512,026 bytes vs 510,272 chars).

R-010's third half says a green local suite is not evidence until you know WHICH checks looked, so the unlooked line was read rather than the exit code taken. task-pipeline `test:all` EXIT=0 with unlooked: 3 — (a) coordination, which reports what it discovered (15 guarded patterns, 4 version surfaces) rather than skipping; (b) backlog citations, 9 spans checked and 6 single-line citations unanchored because one line carries no phrase to compare; (c) routed triggers, the known standalone-checkout limit with no umbrella above it. None is a check that silently switched off, and the one that matters here — the release-gap/run-stamp gate — DID run: it is what refused v1.86.0 and then v1.86.1 until both were declared.

104 broken symlinks across 49 skill channels, invisible to the health check this family documents — that check names five channels and the machine now has ~50, so it reported 0 broken while 104 sat outside its list. Two causes. (1) Eight links in ~/.codex/skills pointed six levels up (../../../../../../) where two are needed: hand-copied between channels, which CLAUDE.md warns about by name ("symlink depth differs per channel — never hand-copy a symlink between channels"). All eight targets existed; only the depth was wrong. Repointed absolutely, matching that channel's own working links. (2) 96 links, exactly two per channel across 48 channels, pointed at ~/.agents/skills/brand-voice-enforcement and ux-copy — the names super-ux used before they became brand-voice and copywriting. The hub entries went with the rename; the channel links did not. Removed. Verified: 0 broken across EVERY channel found by discovery, not by a list.

Reported, NOT changed. ~/.codex/skills holds 51 entries and none of the family's 29; the hub and ~/.kiro/skills carry 28 of 29 (the 29th, "super-ux", is a plugin name, not a skill). Codex IS in skills.json defaultAgents and ~/.codex/AGENTS.md carries the routing block, so Codex knows the routes without reaching the skills. The launcher has a plan for it — `node bin/sshlg-skills.js install --agent codex` renders nine `skills add` steps — and ~/.sshlg-skills/state.json records only routers, so there is no evidence either way about whether this was chosen. This is left for the operator because the family's own doctrine says consumption is deliberately uneven and a skill missing from a channel is usually a choice; installing into a channel someone may have emptied on purpose is a decision, not a debt closure. Also worth recording: my first measurement of this reported 0/29 for EVERY channel, including the hub, because zsh does not word-split an unquoted parameter — a check that reports zero everywhere is likelier broken than the machine being empty, and it was.
